chunks: And from him, from Mūsā ibn al-Ḥasan, from Muḥammad ibn ʿAbd al-Ḥamīd, from Abī Jamīlah al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Zayd al-Shaḥḥām, from Abī ʿAbd Allāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about a man who became junub, then performed ghusl before urinating, then later saw something. He said: “He does not repeat the ghusl; that which he saw is not [necessarily] the discharge in question.”

Its meaning is that if he had exerted effort before the ghusl to urinate, but was unable and it did not become possible for him, then Allah has lifted from him, in that case, the repetition of the ghusl. But as for negligence, then repeating the ghusl becomes necessary, according to what we have mentioned.

key_terms.أَجْنَبَ: became in a state of janabah requiring ghusl
key_terms.اجْتَهَدَ: he exerted effort and tried his best
key_terms.التَّفْرِيطِ: negligence or failure to take due care
key_terms.لَا يُعِيدُ الْغُسْلَ: he does not repeat the ghusl

ai.seo_question: If someone performs ghusl al-janabah before urinating and later sees discharge, must the ghusl be repeated?
ai.summary: This hadith discusses the ruling of a person in janabah who performs ghusl before urinating and later notices something exiting. The text clarifies that if he had tried to urinate before ghusl but was unable to do so, repeating the ghusl is not required; however, if there was negligence, then repeating the ghusl is necessary.
